label: copy-phase input n at middle recall positions (3-5), not last step
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase. It never fires in the original phase or on <DEL>. About 89% of activation mass is on steps where the fed-back input is the letter n. The top examples are all n re-fed as input at recall_idx 3-4, meaning n was original token 2-3, and the strongest ones are in long sequences (L=8-9). It is weak or absent when n appears early in the copy (recall_idx<=2), near the end of the copy (last step), or in short sequences. A small residue of activation comes from other copy-phase inputs, mainly j, o and g. Many copy-phase n steps in the right window stay inactive, so precision is only about 0.55. Dev: P 0.56, R 0.65, F1 0.60, mass recall 0.80.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=10: n, j, g, o; t=12: n, j, o, 2; t=11: n, j, o, 2) and the token being output (most: j, 3, 2, c, i, h; least: y, -, q, m); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4, L=7 & t=10.
